title: Pointwise Minimax Rates for Conditional Cumulative-Incidence Contrasts under Competing Risks

proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a full two-regime upper and lower frontier and honest connected-interval rate on the same bounded-density class. The math reviewer passed with no findings and the general reviewer graded the note field, but D0.5 stopped after three revisions because its decision finding demanded two purported accepted-bank comparators that are actually banked as downgraded. This failed-bank label records the exhausted discovery review, not a mathematical counterexample; any re-raise needs the reviewer-contract defect resolved before review resumes.
tldr: The selected continuous recursion makes the cause-1 cumulative-incidence contrast \(\tau_P(x_0)\) an everywhere-defined observed-law functional, with causal interpretation asserted \(P_X\)-almost everywhere. A midpoint-frozen sequential close-pair response cancels all pilot terms through quadratic order across the fourteen treatment-history cells. Fixed-dimensional endpoint-average pair regression attains the full elbow rate \(n^{-\rho}\), where \(\rho=\min\{r_{\mathrm{pair}},r_0\}\), uniformly over every measurable covariate density between the public bounds. Correlated-sign and localized one-hazard full-history experiments match the pair-limited and saturated branches, so both all-estimator absolute risk and exactly \(0.90\)-honest connected-interval expected length have rate \(n^{-\rho}\) on the identical class. None of the cited public results establishes this displayed same-class two-sided pointwise-risk and honest connected-interval frontier. The benchmark \(d=2\), \(\gamma=1\), and \(\alpha=\eta=\beta=1/6\) has rate \(n^{-1/5}\).
gap: Published competing-risk estimators provide marginal augmented estimating equations, censoring-unbiased transformations, or learner comparisons, while published pointwise minimax CATE and close-pair random-design theory treat ordinary outcomes or conditional variance. None supplies an observed-law version resolution, a sequential score, a same-class full-history converse, and honest pointwise length theory uniformly over all bounded-positive measurable covariate densities.
fill: The project selects unique continuous primitive versions, derives the fourteen-cell cancellation, proves uniform pair-bias and overlap-covariance bounds without a density modulus, constructs a total thresholded estimator and explicit honest interval, and matches them by a legal complete-history experiment on the identical bounded-positive-density class.
